name: Create fee structures, invoices and payments tables
w: Money must never be modelled as a single mutable balance. Invoices plus payments keeps partial payments, corrections and disputes auditable, and integer amounts avoid floating point drift in rent totals.
ac: fee_structures has hostel_id, sharing_type, monthly_amount, effective_from and effective_to

invoices has hostel_id, resident_id, allocation_id, period_month, amount, due_date, status (issued or void) and void_reason, with a unique constraint on resident_id plus period_month for issued invoices
payments has hostel_id, invoice_id, amount, paid_at, mode, reference, recorded_by, voided_at and void_reason
All money columns are integers in paise, not floating point
RLS is enabled on all three tables
Paid, partial, unpaid and overdue are derived in a security_invoker view and never stored
Composite foreign keys keep invoices and payments in the same hostel as their resident and invoice
All three tables are added to the cross-tenant RLS suite
out: No GST computation, no credit notes and no security deposit ledger in the MVP.

name: Implement fee structure setup per sharing type
w: Rents differ by sharing type and change over time. Structures need effective dates so a rent revision does not silently rewrite what last month cost.
ac: Owner sets a monthly amount per sharing type with an effective from date
A new structure never changes already issued invoices
Overlapping structures are resolved by a defined, documented rule
Rooms without a matching structure are flagged clearly rather than silently under-billed
Setup is quick enough for a new hostel during onboarding
Rent precedence is documented: the allocation rent_override first, then the fee structure for the room's sharing type effective on the 1st of the billing month
out: No per-resident negotiated rent UI beyond the allocation rent override.

name: Generate monthly invoices for active residents
w: Manual invoicing is the chore owners hate, but generating duplicates would be worse than doing nothing, so the operation must be safely repeatable.
ac: Generating for a period creates one invoice per resident holding a live allocation
Re-running for the same period creates no duplicates, enforced by the unique constraint rather than app logic alone, and reports what it skipped
Allocations that started mid-month are handled by a defined, documented rule
Rent overrides on the allocation take precedence over the structure amount
A summary reports how many invoices were created and the total value
Runs as one Postgres function call, so a failure leaves no partial batch
An invoice issued in error can be voided with a reason; voided invoices are excluded from balances and the period can be regenerated for that resident
A resident transferred mid-month still gets exactly one invoice for that month, per the documented rule
Billing months and due dates are computed in Asia/Kolkata
out: No proration engine beyond the documented mid-month rule and no automated scheduler.

name: Implement manual payment recording with partial payments
w: Most Indian PGs collect rent by cash, UPI to a personal account or bank transfer. Recording those payments accurately, including partial ones, is the core of the fee product until a gateway exists.
ac: Records amount, mode (cash, UPI, bank transfer, card) date and reference
Partial payments are supported and the derived invoice status reflects them
Paid, partial, unpaid and overdue derive from payments versus amount in the invoice view; no status column is updated
Overpayment beyond the invoice balance is blocked
Payments are never edited or deleted; a mistaken payment is voided with a reason and drops out of all totals
A record-payment action is added to the resident profile and the fee list
out: No payment gateway, no automatic reconciliation and no refunds workflow.

name: Calculate outstanding balance and due status per resident
w: Outstanding dues is the number the owner actually acts on. It must be computed from invoices minus payments so it always reconciles and never needs manual correction.
ac: Outstanding equals total invoiced minus total paid, computed from the database
Overdue is derived from due date plus remaining unpaid balance
A resident with several unpaid months aggregates correctly
A negative balance is never displayed as an amount due
A reconciliation test matches seeded invoices and payments exactly
The resident profile fee section (E5-T5) shows fee history and the outstanding balance
Overdue is evaluated against the current date in Asia/Kolkata
out: No late fee or interest calculation in the MVP.

name: Build fee status list with paid, partial, due and overdue filters
w: This screen replaces the owner's paper register and is the daily driver for rent collection rounds.
ac: Hostel-wide list with running totals per status bucket
Filters by status, room and month, and sorting by outstanding amount
Responsive with 2000 invoices through indexed, paginated queries
Each row links to the resident and to payment recording
Email and phone details are visible so the owner can follow up immediately
out: No bulk WhatsApp or SMS reminders from this screen; that is backlog epic EP-11.

name: Add printable invoice and receipt view
w: Residents and parents ask for proof. A printable page removes the need for the owner to maintain a parallel system just for receipts.
ac: Print-optimised A4 layout with hostel header, resident, period and breakdown
Shows amount paid, balance and payment reference
Browser print to PDF produces a clean document with no menus or chrome
Printing never mutates invoice or payment data
out: No online payment link on the printed invoice, since no gateway exists in the MVP.
